title: Qarmatians
capsule: The Qarmatians (Qaramita) were an Isma'ili Shi'a revolutionary movement that established a communalist state in al-Ahsa, eastern Arabia, founded by Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi in 899. At their height they collected tribute from both the Abbasid caliphate and the Fatimid Imamate, controlled Red Sea and Gulf trade routes, and in 930 sacked Mecca under Abu Tahir al-Jannabi, killing thousands of pilgrims, dumping bodies in the Zamzam Well, and removing the Black Stone to al-Ahsa, where it remained until the Abbasids ransomed it back in 952. A catastrophic false-Mahdi episode in 931 — in which a proclaimed messiah was executed after 80 days — permanently damaged the sect's religious credibility. The Uyunid dynasty, backed by Seljuk forces, ended Qarmatian political control of al-Ahsa around 1067–1077.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Qarmatian state in al-Ahsa is well-attested in Abbasid and Fatimid sources; the geographic extent of their campaigns and tribute zones across Arabia and the Levant is documented but not cartographically precise.
